doc.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023

title: Rock Around the Clock and rock and roll's roots
summary: They argue whether the song swings; he says it predates swing and traces rock and roll to 1921 blues.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Some of the oddities, I don’t know why this came into my head maybe because I play the song “Rock Around the Clock” and —
“Rock Around the Clock” is a swing tune.
Okay, but I’m talking about the feel of it, which is sort of —
Well the feel of it is about screwing to the clock. I mean that’s what the song is about. That’s what rock & roll actually means.

It’s our method of reproduction. I mean the roots for that song, what was his name, J. Berni Barbour — anyway, you know “My Man Rocks Me (With One Steady Roll).” That was out there in 1921. And if the parents who objected to rhythm & blues being re-named rock & roll, if they only knew. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
They would have thrown those 45s out in the garbage.
